text: In prover-estimator debate the prover (Alice) decomposes a problem into subclaims, the estimator (Bob) only assigns probabilities to those subclaims, and the prover uses the probabilities to choose which subclaim to recurse on, unlike earlier protocols where the opponent selects the subclaim to challenge. The authors show Bob can always produce probabilities Alice cannot distinguish from the truth while spending computation not much greater than Alice's, so Alice cannot on average pick a subproblem where Bob is non-trivially wrong.
title: Prover-estimator debate: prover decomposes, estimator assigns subclaim probabilities
